name: Burj Khalifa
headline: height
description: Burj Khalifa in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, completed in 2010, is the world's tallest building. CTBUH measures it at 828 m to its architectural top, which includes the spire, and 829.8 m to its very tip. It has 163 floors above ground, but the highest occupied floor is at 585.4 m, far below the top of the spire.

measures.label: Height (architectural)
measures.note: CTBUH height to architectural top, including the spire but not antennas (2,717 ft)

measures.label: Height to tip
measures.note: CTBUH height to the highest point of the building, including antennas and other functional-technical equipment (2,723 ft)

facts.text: Burj Khalifa has 163 floors above ground and 1 below ground.
Its observatory is 555.7 m above the ground.
Guinness World Records lists it as the tallest building, at 828 m (2,716 ft 6 in).

sources.publisher: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (The Skyscraper Center)
sources.title: Burj Khalifa - The Skyscraper Center

caveats: The commonly quoted 828 m is CTBUH's height to the architectural top, which includes the spire; it is not the height to the tip. CTBUH gives 829.8 m to the tip. The task brief called 828 m the 'to tip' height, which is not correct.
Guinness World Records independently gives 828 m (2,716 ft 6 in), which matches CTBUH's architectural height.
The official site burjkhalifa.ae returned HTTP 403, both live and through the Internet Archive, so no figures were read from it.
